_readme: Reviewed classification of native process exits for scripts/run_isolated_tests.py.
This file is evidence, not a mute button: a file listed here is accepted ONLY when
it also wrote a complete, machine-readable pytest result in which every test passed,
and its process exit code matches the reviewed code below. A listed file that exits
cleanly is a success. A listed file that exits with a different code fails the gate.
An unlisted file that exits natively fails the gate.
Adding a file here requires the same evidence Phase 15 recorded: a complete passing
summary before the fault, and proof the fault is not attributable to current

known_native_exit.condition: A native fault raised in Qt interpreter teardown AFTER pytest printed and wrote a COMPLETE PASSING result. The specific code is environment-dependent: a local Windows box reports 0xC0000005 (STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION), the GitHub windows-latest runner reports 0xC0000409 (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN), and the ubuntu-latest runner reports -11 (SIGSEGV) for the same files, varying run to run. All are the same phenomenon: Qt interpreter teardown after a clean run. The safety property is the complete passing result written before the fault -- the runner enforces that separately, and a native death BEFORE a complete result is never classified here regardless of code.
known_native_exit.evidence: docs/tag-editor/PHASE_15_FINAL_AUDIT.md sections 2.4 and 10.1. 0xC0000005 observed locally; 0xC0000409-at-teardown observed on GitHub Actions windows-latest and -11/SIGSEGV on ubuntu-latest (run 29482330184, PR #3 CI), where the gate correctly REFUSED to accept each unreviewed code until its evidence was recorded. docs/tag-editor/MASTER_PLAN.md records the same behaviour at the Phase 0 baseline (b979147), where it relocated when the blamed file was excluded, proving accumulated Qt state rather than a defective test. tests/test_metadata_io_ui_phase12.py added 2026-07-18/19 after this exact complete-pass-then-SIGSEGV pattern recurred three separate times on ubuntu-latest across unrelated docs/scraper PRs (#66, #67, #70) with an empty diff for this file each time, and a rerun passed cleanly every time -- the same accumulated-Qt-teardown-state phenomenon, just not yet individually classified for this file.
known_native_exit.distinct_from_retry: This teardown 0xC0000409 (complete result written first) is NOT the F-11 converter condition below, which is a MID-RUN 0xC0000409 with no complete result. The complete_result flag is what separates them.

intermittent_native_retry.condition: A native crash raised MID-RUN, before any summary, roughly one run in six. Environment-dependent code, like the teardown class above: STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN (0xC0000409) on Windows, SIGSEGV (-11) on macOS/Linux. No complete result is written, so the file is retried rather than classified. Accepted only when a later attempt produces a clean, complete, passing result; a logical failure is never retried.
intermittent_native_retry.evidence: docs/tag-editor/PHASE_15_INITIAL_AUDIT.md finding F-11 - reproduced 1-in-6 at 8d2c497 and 2-in-6 at the pre-Phase-14 base 711f0c3, with an empty diff for the converter files across Phase 14, proving it pre-dates the current code. The macOS SIGSEGV manifestation was observed on the release-macos.yml dispatch run 29505337809 (converter passed cleanly on the prior macOS dispatch 29500668760), confirming the same non-determinism.
